description: The literal forms of the COPY statement's library-text name and library name (ISO §2023:7.2.3.2: COPY { text-name-1 | literal-1 } [ { OF | IN } { library-name-1 | literal-2 } ]; §2023:7.2.3.3 SR4/SR5 restrict them to alphanumeric literals; §2023:7.2.3.4 GR1 "Text-name-1 or literal-1 identifies the library text"). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 general format is COPY text-name-1 [ { OF | IN } library-name-1 ] [ REPLACING ... ] (§1985:XII.2.2), both names user-defined words (§1985:III.2: text-name, 'A user-defined word which identifies library text'; library-name, 'A user-defined word that names a COBOL library'), and §1985:XII.2.4 GR2 copies 'the library text associated with text-name-1 is copied into the source program'; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 adds literal-1 and literal-2 (§2002:7.1.2.2 SR5: 'Literal-1 and literal-2 shall be alphanumeric literals'; §2002:7.1.2.3 GR1: 'Text-name-1 or literal-1 identifies the library text') and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 37: 'COPY statement. An alphanumeric literal may be specified in place of text-name-1 or library-name-1.' 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.2.2.3 GR1). VCR row 7.44. ONE gate for both literals, CopyProcessor.GateCopyPhrase (kb/Work PB1601).
display: a literal COPY library-text name or library name
vcr: §2002:7.1.2.2 SR5 / §2002:F.2 literal-1 / literal-2; the edge quoted from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965); VCR row 7.44
